weight_plan.notes: Steady loss from 78 kg on 9 Nov 2026 to 60 kg on Sunday 2 May 2027 (3 weeks before the 23 May taper), then hold 60 kg through race day. This is the current target; an earlier plan aimed at 70 kg by 31 May and is no longer the target.

baselines.easy_run_source: Median of 14 runs in the last 28 days.
baselines.bike_notes: Use 17.49 km/h as the primary bike starting point (outdoor average excluding a 24 Oct ride at 10.6 km/h). The official last-28-day distance-weighted baseline is 15.16 km/h (n=7), pulled down by that ride. Do not use indoor/virtual trainer speed as the outdoor race baseline, and do not use a 20 km/h claim as the race start.
baselines.swim_notes: Baseline is only 2 pool swims, including wall rests: 603 m in 40.8 min and 558 m in 40.7 min, raw about 7:01/100 m. Projected race swim paces below already include a race adjustment. Weight does not change the swim projection.

model_notes: Fitness curve is an assumption, not a specific study: central 6.5%/month for the first 3 months, easing to 1.5% by 1 Apr 2027; optimistic 8%→2%; conservative 3%→1%.
Bike speed scales about with power^(1/3).
Weight effect rule of thumb: run ~1% faster pace per 1% body mass lost; bike (flat) ~0.2% per 1% lost; swim no weight effect.
Off-the-bike half = easy pace × 1.05 / 1.08 / 1.12 (opt / central / cons).
Cutoffs: swim 1.9 km in 1h10; usual swim+T1+bike ~5h30; finish 8h30.
Primary displayed scenario is 60 kg on 2 May 2027 + fairer bike start 17.49 km/h.

weight_only_60kg_bike_15_16.label: 60 kg, official bike start 15.16 km/h
weight_only_60kg_bike_15_16.notes: Same 60 kg weight plan, but starting from the official 15.16 km/h outdoor baseline. Swim times match the primary scenario.

honesty: Even the optimistic primary total (8:17) has a swim of 1:31, which is still over the 1h10 swim cutoff.
The central total (8:48) is still over the 8h30 finish cutoff, and the optimistic swim+bike (5:56) is still over the usual ~5h30 cutoff.
Durban is currently aimed at a first finish and the cutoffs, not a 6:30 target.
